summary.title: Fix identity first, then act on segments
summary.subhead: Acme Retail (test) wants one connected customer view, and a license renewal sets the deadline.
summary.challenge: Data is siloed across channels, and cross-device behavior cannot be seen. Drop-off between consideration and purchase is visible, but the team does not fully trust the segment data.
summary.opportunity: Modernize measurement in stages. Strengthen identity first, rebuild priority segments on connected data, and then add journey analysis and a unified identity graph.
summary.outcomes: Faster decisions and an improved customer experience, with personalization and better segmentation as the main drivers.
summary.findings: Three of six readiness areas are developing and three need attention: data & architecture, insights & measurement, and activation & actionability.
summary.decision: Sponsor agreement on priorities, a confirmed renewal date, and a clear owner for next steps.

readiness.title: Three areas developing, three need attention
readiness.subhead: Identity, governance, and people are developing, and data, insights, and activation need attention.

rows.evidence: 4 of 24 items are tracked, all low complexity. Visitor ID, CRM ID, orders, and cart adds were not marked as tracked.
A deterministic login stitch is in place. The target is a unified identity graph, two stages away.
Data is siloed, cross-device behavior is not visible, and segment data is not fully trusted.
Segment changes take days to notice. Next-step ownership is unclear, and the team has a skills gap.
Access controls and consent governance are in place. Governance labels and usage labels are gaps.
All four roles have named owners, and the model is hybrid. External support and skills are needed.

readiness.attention: Visibility of tracked data, cross-device identity, trust in segments, and ownership of next steps.
readiness.discovery: Which untracked items are in use. Whether visitor and customer IDs are captured. Which tools consume segments.

objectives.subhead: The team wants faster decisions and a better experience through personalization and segmentation.

rows.challenge: Data is siloed across channels, and cross-device behavior cannot be seen.

rows.value: Fewer blind spots and a base for every later use case.

rows.challenge: Segment drop-off is visible, but the team does not fully trust the data.
rows.outcome: Priority segments rebuilt on connected data and tied to personalization.

objectives.note: Objectives are ordered by how strongly the workshop answers support them.

gaps.title: Four gaps stand between data and action
gaps.subhead: Identity, trust in segments, governance labels, and ownership of next steps need to close first.

rows.gap: Identity does not yet span devices
rows.why: Cross-device behavior cannot be seen, so one person can look like several.
rows.response: Register identity namespaces, set stitching priority, and extend in stages. A unified graph needs Real-Time CDP, to be validated.

rows.why: Drop-off between consideration and purchase is visible, but the team does not fully trust the data.
rows.response: Rebuild priority segments on connected data and document the intent of each. Depends on a segment inventory.

rows.why: Governance labels and usage labels are gaps. Connecting more data without them could add risk.
rows.response: Design labels with the schema and review them before identity is extended. Depends on the IT and governance admin.

rows.gap: Next steps have no clear owner
rows.why: Segment changes take days to notice, and a skills gap slows action.
rows.response: Define workflows and owners for acting on segments, and plan external support. The tools that consume segments are not yet known.

target.subhead: A connected foundation lets Acme Retail (test) move from siloed data to confident action.

opportunities.title: Three opportunities for measurable value
opportunities.subhead: Each ties a current challenge to a capability and a measure the team can baseline today.

items.name: Drop-off visibility
items.challenge: Most people are lost between consideration and purchase, and cross-device behavior is hidden.
items.capability: A journey view across touchpoints that shows where people stall.
items.objective: Reduce drop-off between consideration and purchase.
items.prerequisites: Data schema, Web SDK, and identity namespaces for login.

items.name: Priority segments
items.challenge: Segment data is not fully trusted, and changes take days to notice.
items.capability: Rebuilt segments (started but not finished, high-value, and multi-channel engaged) on stitched identity.
items.kpi: Time to notice a segment change (days today). Baseline required.
items.prerequisites: Segment inventory, identity stitching, and governance labels.

items.name: Unified identity graph
items.challenge: A login stitch covers known customers only, and cross-device behavior is hidden.
items.capability: A graph that resolves every identifier into one person across devices and channels.
items.objective: Improve the customer experience across touchpoints.
items.kpi: Cross-device journeys linked to one person. Baseline required.
items.prerequisites: Real-Time CDP, consent in the identity graph, and offline sources connected.

opportunities.note: No improvement targets are shown. Baselines come first.

roadmap.title: Three stages with a decision between each
roadmap.subhead: The sequence follows the typical path from foundation to parity to expansion, with no dates set.

stages.name: Foundation
bullets: Implement the Web and Mobile SDK
Build and validate the first Data View

stages.name: Parity
bullets: Run Adobe Analytics and Customer Journey Analytics in parallel

stages.name: Expansion
bullets: Extend identity toward a unified graph
Retire Adobe Analytics reporting once parity is confirmed

gates: Gate after stage 1: approve priorities and owners.
Gate before retiring Adobe Analytics reporting: confirm parity.
roadmap.note: Stages are typical and are not scheduled, sized, or approved. The renewal date is an input to the sequence.

team.title: What it takes on the team's side
team.subhead: Roles, owners, and technical groups the team needs to line up before any build starts.
roles: IT and governance admin: Casey Moore
team.ownership: Next steps after insight have no clear owner, and an executive sponsor is not yet named.
team.complexity: 4 tracked items retain and map. Of the 20 untracked items, 6 retain and map, 9 reconfigure or rebuild, and 5 extend. Use of each needs confirming.
team.governance: Governance labels and usage labels are gaps. Access controls and consent governance need review as identity extends.
team.enablement: Hybrid operating model. External support is needed for change management and training, and a skills gap slows action.
team.note: Findings are preliminary and subject to technical validation. This document is not a statement of work or contractual commitment.

identity.subhead: Where the team is today, where it wants to be, and what has to be true in between.

rows.current: Deterministic login stitch. Visitor ID and CRM ID were not marked as tracked, which needs confirming.
rows.target: Unified identity graph, reached through cross-channel stitching of mobile and offline data.
rows.dependencies: Mobile and offline sources connected. Real-Time CDP provisioned and consent integrated into the graph. Licensing and product support to be validated.

rows.current: Access controls and consent governance are in place. Governance labels and usage labels are gaps.
rows.target: All four controls in place and owned before identity is extended.
rows.dependencies: Labels designed with the schema, usage policies set for activation, and input from the IT and governance admin.

identity.note: Governance controls are enforced at the field level by Adobe Experience Platform. Consent flags are stored against the identity graph and checked before data is used downstream.

left.definition: The web and app reporting tool the team uses today.
Adobe's reporting tool that joins data from every channel into one view of each person.
Custom tracking fields in Adobe Analytics.
The anonymous ID Adobe uses to recognize a browser or device before someone logs in.
A map that connects every known ID back to one person.
Adobe's platform for building and activating audiences in real time.

right.definition: An agreed structure for how data is named and stored.
Newer data collection code for the website and the app.
The set of fields and measures the team reports on in CJA.
A labeled type of ID, such as the visitor ID or the CRM customer ID.
Deterministic matching uses a known ID such as a login. Probabilistic matching uses statistical signals.
Today's number for a measure, used to compare against later.
